You are an assistant that will act like a person. I will play the role of a Linux (Ubuntu) operating system.
Your goal is to implement the operations required by me or answer the questions proposed by me.
For each of your turns, you should first think about what you should do, and then call exactly one of the provided tools according to the situation.
If you think the output is too long, I will truncate it. The truncated output is not complete. You have to deal with the truncating problem by yourself.
Attention, your bash code should not contain any input operation. Once again, you should use one tool in each turn, and should not respond without function calling.
Prefer short, simple bash commands. Avoid large multi-line scripts unless the task explicitly asks you to create a script or file.
For query tasks, prefer one short read-only command; as soon as shell output contains the exact answer, call answer_action immediately.
For state-change tasks, prefer one minimal change and then one short verification command.
Note that if you think the task has been finished, or there is some message missing to completely complete the task, you should respond with calling the function "finish_action", as no additional information will be provided.
Also, note that if you have gotten the answer to the question, you should call the "answer_action" tool instead of simply writing your answer in your response.
Your answers should be exact and precise (for example, a single number), do not answer with full sentences or phrases.
Always use a tool provided instead of simply responding with content.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_checks" to hold all intermediate artifacts for this procedure.  
2. Capture and save a current snapshot of /working (its top-level metadata) into "temp_workspace_checks/original_state.txt".  
3. Produce a full recursive listing of /working and save the raw listing to "temp_workspace_checks/raw_listing.txt".  
4. From the raw listing, extract every entry whose filename is exactly "workspace" and save those candidate paths to "temp_workspace_checks/matches_candidates.txt".  
5. For each candidate path, collect filesystem metadata (type, size, permissions, owner) and append results to "temp_workspace_checks/type_checks.txt".  
6. Normalize and deduplicate the candidate paths from the type checks, writing the unique resolved path list to "temp_workspace_checks/unique_candidates.txt".  
7. For each unique candidate, resolve any references (such as links) and record the final target path and its resolved metadata to "temp_workspace_checks/resolved_candidates.txt".  
8. Produce a concise summary that notes which resolved targets are regular files and record this per-path verdict into "temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt", including any permission or access errors encountered.  
9. Load "temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt", set a decision placeholder that maps the presence of any regular-file verdict to a single-line result, and prepare to emit that single-line result while leaving all intermediate artifacts intact for audit.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

function.arguments:
{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace_checks
ls -ld /working > temp_workspace_checks/original_state.txt
ls -laR /working > temp_workspace_checks/raw_listing.txt
find /working -name "workspace" > temp_workspace_checks/matches_candidates.txt
touch temp_workspace_checks/type_checks.txt
while IFS= read -r f; do
  ls -ld "$f" >> temp_workspace_checks/type_checks.txt || true
done < temp_workspace_checks/matches_candidates.txt
sort -u temp_workspace_checks/matches_candidates.txt > temp_workspace_checks/unique_candidates.txt
touch temp_workspace_checks/resolved_candidates.txt
while IFS= read -r f; do
  res=$(readlink -f "$f")
  echo "$res" >> temp_workspace_checks/resolved_candidates.txt
  ls -ld "$res" >> temp_workspace_checks/resolved_candidates.txt || true
done < temp_workspace_checks/unique_candidates.txt
touch temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt
while IFS= read -r f; do
  res=$(readlink -f "$f")
  if [ -f "$res" ] && [ ! -L "$res" ]; then
    echo "$res is a regular file" >> temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt
  else
    echo "$res is not a regular file" >> temp_workspace_checks/summary.txt
  fi
done < temp_workspace_checks/unique_candidates.txt

find /working -type f -name "workspace"
"}
function.name: bash_action
